setup-hardware-deep-cluster-one-week: Section IV-C, p.7 to 8: 12 DEEP nodes (checked in the PDF text: the 12 ends p.7), each 2 Xeon 8260M and a V100, about a week in total.

fidelity-kernels-classically-simulable-l: coordinator sign-off: the narrowing is right; the clause on projected quantum kernels is cited to [9] and is removed from the value (sign-off value_replace), leaving the limit the paper states on its own kernels, HIGH as stored; the reviewer's reason for LOW was: Section I, p.1 to 2: the narrowed value matches the text. But it holds two claims. The first is a stated limit. The second, that projected quantum kernels remain classically intractable, is a field statement cited to [9]. Graded by the weaker, so a drop from the stored HIGH for the team lead to decide.

theory_low.cost-of-all-parameter-derivatives-2-n-th: Section 3.2, p.11: a one-sentence assertion with no derivation. Not a proved result.
theory_low.theorem-2-2-2-smoothed-lipschitz: Theorem 2.2.2, p.4 to 5: the proof uses Theorem 2.2.1, which is [14, Theorem 1], and says the l2 case is proved in [14]. It rests on a cited result from [14].
theory_low.lemma-2-2-3-sampling-error-gradient-boun: Lemma 2.2.3, p.5 to 6: the proof starts from Theorem 2.2.1, which is [14, Theorem 1]. It rests on a cited result from [14].
theory_low.quantum-small-sigma-increases-sampling-e: Section 2.2, p.6: an upper bound grows as sigma falls. The text then concludes the error impact rises. A bound's growth does not show the error grows, and it rests on Lemma 2.2.3, which rests on [14].
theory_low.optimised-parameter-shift-two-versus-thr: Section 2.4.3, p.9: rules (2.5) and (2.6) come from the parameter shift rule of [21, Equation 9] and the paper says they are covered in [21]. A cited result, with a count read off it.
theory_low.theorem-2-4-4-dth-derivative-parameter-s: Theorem 2.4.4, p.9 to 10: the proof is repeated use of the parameter shift rule (2.4), taken from [21, Equation 9]. It rests on a specific cited result. Boundary case: (2.4) follows from Lemma 2.4.3, but the paper does not derive it.
theory_low.lemma-3-3-1-complexity-prototypical-loss: Lemma 3.3.1, p.12 to 13: the count uses the basic parameter shift rule (2.4), cited to [21, Equation 9]. It rests on a specific cited result. Boundary case as for Theorem 2.4.4.
theory_low.lemma-3-3-2-complexity-variational-loss: Lemma 3.3.2, p.14: the count uses the basic parameter shift rule (2.4), cited to [21, Equation 9]. Boundary case as for Theorem 2.4.4.
theory_low.lemma-3-3-3-complexity-gaussian-smoothed: Lemma 3.3.3, p.14 to 15: the proof uses the Hessian estimator (3.13) 'as proven in [14]' and the control variate 'just as authors do in [14]'. It rests on a result from [14].
theory_low.lemma-3-3-4-complexity-smoothed-variatio: Lemma 3.3.4, p.15: the proof is 'proceeding as in the proof of Lemma 3.3.3' and uses the gradient estimator of [14, Theorem 1]. It rests on results from [14].
theory_low.lemma-3-3-5-complexity-poisson: Lemma 3.3.5, p.15: the proof reuses the Lemma 3.3.1 and 3.3.2 decomposition, which uses the parameter shift rule (2.4) from [21, Equation 9]. Boundary case as for Theorem 2.4.4.
theory_low.lemma-3-3-6-complexity-gaussian-poisson: Lemma 3.3.6, p.16: the proof takes the Gaussian Laplacian from [14, Equation 11]. It rests on a cited result from [14].
theory_low.lemma-3-4-1-complexity-heat: Lemma 3.4.1, p.16: two claims. The first uses the parameter shift rule (2.4) from [21]. The Gaussian statement uses the estimator (3.16) from [14]. Graded by the weaker.
theory_low.lemma-3-5-1-complexity-hjb: Lemma 3.5.1, p.17: two claims. The first uses the parameter shift rule (2.4) from [21]. The Gaussian statement uses (3.16) from [14]. Graded by the weaker.
theory_low.section-3-6-explicit-complexity-polynomi: Section 3.6, p.17 to 18: the arithmetic is right (checked: 72d^4+141d^3+87d^2+18d and 6d^3+9d^2+3d+1) but it substitutes into Lemmas 3.3.1 and 3.3.2, which rest on the cited parameter shift rule [21]. The alpha_i counts are stated, not derived.
theory_low.section-3-6-variational-better-scaling: Section 3.6, p.18: the comparison follows from the two polynomials, which rest on Lemmas 3.3.1 and 3.3.2 (cited parameter shift rule [21]). 'Clearly better scaling' is stated, not shown. Graded with its source.
theory_low.section-3-6-smoothing-thresholds-k-1024: Section 3.6, p.18: the thresholds d at least 9 and 10 are stated with no derivation (the arithmetic checks out) and use the K(5nr+ne) and K(3nr+ne) counts, which rest on [14]. K = 1024 is chosen from the range reported in [14].
theory_low.section-3-7-lipschitz-constant-3n: Section 3.7, p.18 to 19: the 3n bound on the output is simple, but the Lipschitz constant 3n/sigma sqrt(2/pi) comes from Theorem 2.2.2, which rests on [14]. Two claims, graded by the weaker.
theory_low.section-3-8-1-heat-small-lipschitz-condi: Section 3.8.1, p.19: the condition on sigma uses the Section 3.7 constant (rests on [14]). The sigma at most 0.1 value is a result outlined in [14]. A cited result.
theory_low.section-3-8-2-heat-large-lipschitz-intra: Section 3.8.2, p.19 to 20: the bound 22360 is a computed value on the paper's example, but the 900 qubits figure uses the Section 3.7 restriction (rests on [14]) and 'intractable' is the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.qfim-diagonal-cost-2p-circuits-tfim: Section II-D, p.5: an informal counting argument in discussion, with no formal statement or proof. Not a proved result.
theory_low.gradient-cost-4mp-circuits: Section II-D, p.5: a count asserted with no derivation and no citation.
theory_low.qfim-diagonal-entry-worst-case-measureme: Section II-D, p.5: an informal cost estimate (order-of-magnitude counting), not a theorem with a proof.
theory_low.qfim-full-measurement-cost-upper-bound: Section II-D, p.5: an informal counting bound in discussion, no formal proof.
theory_low.qfim-estimated-each-step-impractical-lar: Section II-D, p.5: the authors' interpretation of an informal cost count. The 'more feasible' diagonal claim is a comparison with no data.

value_replace.fidelity-kernels-classically-simulable-l: The authors state that the fact these fidelity kernels can be simulated classically undermines their potential to deliver a robust quantum advantage, and that this limitation applies only to the family of fidelity kernels with low-entangling circuits.
